questions.q: What natural role does CRISPR serve in bacteria?
questions.why: CRISPR is a bacterial defense mechanism against viruses.

questions.q: Which disease has CRISPR been used to treat, according to the book?
questions.why: CRISPR has been applied to treat congenital blindness.

questions.q: Why is large‑scale use of CRISPR on human embryos currently limited?
questions.why: Unintended DNA changes could cause birth defects.

questions.q: What ethical concern does the book raise about CRISPR?
questions.why: Some view CRISPR as a tool to shape children per parents' wishes.

questions.q: What future threat does biohacking pose, according to the author?
questions.why: Biohacking could become a major threat to security and privacy.
